title: PEEP versus recruitment of shunt
subtitle: Effect of positive end-expiratory pressure on alveolar derecruitment and shunt fraction in ARDS
ruleBasedNote: Lung recruitment as a function of end-expiratory pressure is a rule-based teaching approximation in Engine v1.

patient.summary: A 52-year-old mechanically ventilated patient with early acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and recruitable atelectasis receiving lung-protective ventilation.

prediction.question: When PEEP is titrated upward from 5 to 14 cmH2O in this patient with recruitable ARDS, how do PaO2, P/F ratio, and static plateau pressure (Pplat) respond?

whatToLookAtHint: Monitor the arterial oxygenation indices (PaO2 and P/F ratio) alongside the static end-inspiratory airway pressure (Pplat).

reflection.question: Why does raising PEEP from 5 to 14 cmH2O markedly improve PaO2 and P/F ratio in this ARDS patient?

options.text: Sustained end-expiratory pressure exceeds alveolar closing and opening thresholds, reopening collapsed lung units and reducing true shunt from 40% down toward 17%.
PEEP converts West lung zone 3 into zone 1, eliminating pulmonary capillary perfusion and enhancing gas exchange.
Higher PEEP stimulates acute de novo surfactant synthesis in type II pneumocytes within seconds.
Higher airway pressure automatically increases tidal volume and doubles minute ventilation in volume-controlled modes.

reflection.explanation: In recruitable ARDS, dependent alveolar units collapse at end-expiration under low PEEP (5 cmH2O), producing severe shunt (40%). Increasing PEEP to 14 cmH2O provides sufficient end-expiratory stent to prevent cyclical collapse and reopen unstable alveoli (recruitment). Over several minutes (tau = 120 s in the engine), recruited fraction rises to ~0.78, cutting effective shunt to ~16.6% and dramatically improving PaO2 and P/F ratio. Concurrently, static plateau pressure increases proportionally with PEEP.

evidence.claim: Higher PEEP levels improve arterial oxygenation and reduce mortality in moderate-to-severe ARDS through recruitment of collapsed alveoli.
evidence.source: Briel M, Meade M, Mercat A, et al. Higher vs lower positive end-expiratory pressure in patients with acute lung injury and acute respiratory distress syndrome: systematic review and meta-analysis. JAMA 2010; 303(9):865-873.

evidence.claim: Titration of PEEP in recruitable ARDS reduces venous admixture and stabilizes end-expiratory lung volume while increasing plateau pressure.
evidence.source: Papazian L, Aubron C, Brochard L, et al. Formal guidelines: management of acute respiratory distress syndrome. Ann Intensive Care 2019; 9(1):69.
